description: The U.S. Offshore Pipeline and Reported Incident Datasets describe the network of existing, decommissioned and abandoned oil and gas pipelines in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico and the incidents reported on them. The Energy Data eXchange page of the National Energy Technology Laboratory, read on 2026-09-28, describes more than 80,000 points along the pipelines, each matched in space and time with structural characteristics, geology and seafloor conditions, meteorological, oceanographic and biochemical statistics and incidents in the same lease block during the pipeline's life, delivered as a file geodatabase and a CSV file, plus an incidents table of more than 900 reported incidents from 1986 to 2021 with causes, costs, repairs, inspections and severity metrics, and field dictionaries. The 2024 data article counts more than 490 attributes drawn from public sources such as BSEE pipeline data and PHMSA incident files. Coverage is the U.S. Gulf of Mexico outer continental shelf. The data are free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence on EDX. Caveats: attributes are matched to points by location and lease block, not observed at each point, and the incident match by lease block may pair incidents with the wrong pipeline. It supports offshore pipeline integrity and hazard studies, such as relating hurricane loading and seafloor instability to incident rates for decommissioning or reuse decisions. No related offshore pipeline incident record is catalogued.
